extracted.intended_audience: intending patent applicants and patent agents in the United Kingdom (1883 rules/instructions)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formal requirements for making, prosecuting, opposing, amending, and registering patent applications and related documents under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act 1883 and its Rules. Covers drawings, affidavits, notices, fees, evidence, oppositions, amendments, compulsory licences, payments and register entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition notice and identification (industrial/international)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desirous of exhibiting an invention at an industrial or international exhibition, or of publishing any description of the invention during the period of the national holding of the exhibition, or of using the invention for the purpose of the exhibition in the place where the exhibition is held, shall, after having obtained from the Board of Trade a certificate that the exhibition is an industrial or international one, give to the Comptroller seven days' notice of his intention to exhibit, publish, or use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For identifying the invention in the event of a subsequent patent application the applicant shall furnish to the Comptroller a brief description accompanied, if necessary, by drawings and such other information as the Comptroller may require. (See S.57 for Board of Trade certificate.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller power to amend documents and correct irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document for the amending of which no special provision is made by the Act may be amended, and any irregularity in procedure which, in the opinion of the Comptroller, may be obviated without detriment to the interests of any person, may be corrected on such terms as the Comptroller may think fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule may not authorize amendment of Letters Patent themselves; see notes to Ss. 18, 91.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by post deemed delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application, notice, or other document required to be left, made, or given at the Patent Office or to the Comptroller may be sent by prepaid letter through the post and, if so sent, shall be deemed to have been left, made, or given at the time when the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prove service it is sufficient to prove that the letter was properly addressed and put into the post. (This Rule forms S. 97 of the Act.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted modes and places for affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits may, except where otherwise prescribed, be used as evidence when sworn in specified ways: (1) in the UK before any person authorized to administer oaths in the Supreme Court of Judicature or before a justice of the peace for the county/place; (2) in British dominions out of UK before any court, judge, or justice of the peace or any person authorized to administer oaths in any court; (3) out of British dominions before a British minister, consul, vice-consul, person exercising their functions, a notary public, or a judge or magistrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Instructions and note that in some cases a notary may also be acceptable (L. T., Feb. 9th, 1884).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory declarations made abroad (form requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any statutory declaration prescribed by the Rules is made out of the United Kingdom the words 'and by virtue of the Statutory Declarations Act, 1835' must be omitted, and the declaration shall be made in the manner prescribed in Rule 20(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also note to Patent Forms A, A1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application opening and numbering order
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications sent by prepaid letter shall, as far as practicable, be opened and numbered in the order in which the letters containing them have been delivered in the ordinary course of post; applications left at the Patent Office otherwise than through the post shall be similarly numbered in order of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule regulates office business and does not determine questions of priority between applications made on the same day; the Act does not recognize fractions of a day and Letters Patent are sealed as of the day of application (S. 18). Opening earlier on the same day does not give priority to bring the second application under S. 7 subs. (6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple inventions in one application (division after refusal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application includes by mistake, inadvertence, or otherwise more than one invention, the applicant may, after refusal by the Comptroller to accept the application, amend it to apply to one invention only and may make application for separate patents for each such invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every such (divided) application shall bear the date of the first application and shall be proceeded with as if originally made on that date for one invention only. Separate fees are payable on each invention. (See S. 7.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by legal representative of deceased
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent by the legal representative of a person who has died possessed of an invention shall be accompanied by an official copy of or extract from his will or the letters of administration in proof of the applicant's title as legal representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S. 12 subs. (8) for rights of legal personal representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and advertisement on acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: On the acceptance of an application with a provisional or complete specification the Comptroller shall give notice to the applicant and shall advertise such acceptance in the official journal of the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of an application with provisional specification gives provisional protection (S. 14); acceptance of a complete specification gives protection by complete specification (S. 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection on publication of acceptance (complete specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication of the advertisement of acceptance in the case of an application with a complete specification, the application and specification with drawings (if any) may be inspected at the Patent Office upon payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S. 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form for communications from abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent for an invention communicated from abroad shall be made in the form A1 set forth in the Second Schedule; the person to whom the invention is communicated is the applicant within the meaning of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing sizes and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings accompanying provisional or complete specifications shall be made upon half-sheets or sheets of imperial drawing paper within a border line of 19 inches by 12 inches, or 27 inches by 19 inches, with a margin of 1/2 an inch all round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also Rule 31 for additional illustrative drawing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of drawings: materials and ink requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the drawings will be required upon rolled imperial drawing paper or upon thin Bristol board of the same dimensions as the original; all lines must be absolutely black, Indian ink of the best quality to be used, and the same strength or colour of the ink maintained throughout the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any shading must be in lines clearly and distinctly drawn and as open as consistent with the required effect; section lines should not be too closely drawn; no colour must be used on the copy; letters and figures of reference must be bold and distinct; the border line should be one fine line only; drawings must not be folded but delivered flat or rolled on a roller so as to be free from creases or breaks. This rule must be strictly observed to allow correct photo-lithographic copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification and drawing preparation after provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete specification is left at the Patent Office after a provisional specification has been accepted the complete specification and drawings accompanying the same, as well as the copy thereof, must be prepared in accordance with Rules 10, 28, and 29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See note to S. 5 as to relation of drawings to the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative drawing of features of novelty (16 sq. inches limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant shall, in addition to the drawings furnished with his complete specification, furnish the Comptroller with a drawing illustrative of the feature or features of novelty constituting his invention; such drawing must not cover a space exceeding 16 square inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The drawing must be prepared in the manner prescribed for the copy of the original drawings but not exceeding 16 square inches and must be accompanied by a concise explanatory statement on foolscap paper legibly written or printed. S.10 gives the Comptroller power to publish an illustrated journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and contents of notice of opposition to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of opposition to the grant of a patent shall state the ground or grounds on which the opponent intends to oppose the grant, and shall be signed by him; it shall state his address for service in the United Kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Form of Notice see Patents Forms, D. Fee payable by opponent noted in First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of notice of opposition furnished to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of a notice of opposition a copy thereof shall be furnished by the Comptroller to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also S. 11 subs. (2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars required where prior patent ground alleged
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ground of opposition is that the invention has been patented in this country on an application of prior date, the title, number and date of the patent granted in such prior application shall be specified in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For grounds of opposition generally see S. 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opponent's evidence timing (statutory declarations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days after the expiration of two months' advertisement of the acceptance of a complete specification, the opponent shall leave at the Patent Office statutory declarations in support of his opposition and deliver to the applicant a list thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 20 regarding form of statutory declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's and opponent's reply evidence timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 14 days from delivery of the opponent's list the applicant shall leave statutory declarations in answer and deliver a list; within seven days from such delivery the opponent shall leave statutory declarations in reply, confined to matters strictly in reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of these declarations may be obtained from the Patent Office or from the opposite party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing evidence and further evidence by leave
rubrics_metrics.description: No further evidence shall be left on either side except by leave of the Comptroller upon the written consent of the parties duly notified to him, or by special leave of the Comptroller on application made to him for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application for leave must be notified to the opposite party who is entitled to oppose the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing after completion of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: On completion of the evidence the Comptroller shall appoint a time for the hearing of the case and shall give to the parties seven days' notice at least of such appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of opposition limited to those stated in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: On the hearing of the case no opposition shall be allowed in respect of any ground not stated in the notice of opposition; if the ground is prior patent, opposition shall not be allowed unless the title, number and date of the prior patent have been duly specified in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For grounds of opposition see S. 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision and right of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the Comptroller in the case shall be notified by him to the parties; either party may appeal to a law officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S. 11 subs. (2) for appeal procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of payment/renewal notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee intends at the expiration of the fourth or eighth year from the date of his patent to make the prescribed payment for keeping it in force, he shall seven days at least before such expiration give notice to the Comptroller of such intention and shall, before the expiration, leave at the Patent Office a form of certificate of payment, duly stamped, with the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and exact fees referenced in Patents Forms J; the acceptance and records relate to preservation of patent term (see Rule 45).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative annual fee payments in lieu of lump sums
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee intends to pay annual fees in lieu of the above-mentioned fees, he shall seven days at least before the expiration of the fourth and each succeeding year during the term of the patent until and inclusive of the 13th year give notice to the Comptroller and shall leave at the Patent Office a form of certificate of payment, duly stamped, with the fee prescribed to be paid at such periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For list of fees payable see First Schedule to these Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of payment and register entry
rubrics_metrics.description: On due compliance with the Rules the Comptroller shall give to the patentee a certificate that the prescribed payment has been duly made; a record of the amount and time of payment will be entered on the Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of certificate in Patents Forms, J.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlargement of time for payments — application content and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for an enlargement of time for making a prescribed payment shall state in detail the circumstances in which the patentee by accident, mistake or inadvertence has failed to make such payment; the Comptroller may require the patentee to substantiate by such proof as he may think necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees payable on enlarging time: for one month £3, two months £7, eight months £10. See S. 17 subs. (8),(4) as to powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller discretion to enlarge time for acts
rubrics_metrics.description: The time prescribed by the Rules for doing any act or taking any proceeding may be enlarged by the Comptroller if he thinks fit, upon such notice to other parties and upon such terms as he may direct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for leave to amend specification (form & advertisement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for leave to amend a specification shall be signed by the applicant or patentee and accompanied by a copy of the original specification and drawings showing in red ink the proposed amendment; it shall be advertised by publication of the request and the nature of the proposed amendment in the official journal of the Patent Office and in such other manner as the Comptroller may direct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Rules do not apply to amendment of clerical errors (see S. 91). For form see Patents Forms, F. As to amendment of specification see S. 18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to amendment: notice and evidence timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of opposition to the amendment shall state the ground or grounds and be signed and state address for service in the UK; on receipt a copy is furnished to the applicant/patentee; within 14 days after expiration of one month from first advertisement the opponent shall leave statutory declarations in support and deliver a list; thereafter Rules 36–39 apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form of notice for opposition to amendment in Patents Forms, G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file amended specification and drawings if leave given
rubrics_metrics.description: Where leave to amend is given the applicant shall, if the Comptroller so requires and within a time to be limited by him, leave at the Patent Office a new specification and drawings as amended, to be prepared in accordance with Rules 10, 28, and 29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where request is made pursuant to a Court order an official or verified copy of the order shall be left with the request (Rule 55). Every amendment shall be advertised by the Comptroller in the official journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licence petition content and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to the Board of Trade for an order upon a patentee to grant a licence shall show clearly the nature of the petitioner's interest, the ground(s) upon which he claims relief, and shall state in detail the circumstances of the case, the terms asked for and the purport of the proposed order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition and examined copy must be left at the Patent Office accompanied by affidavits, statutory declarations and other documentary evidence tendered in proof of alleged default. Forms in Patents Forms H and HI. Petitioner should make out a prima facie case before giving patentee notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timetable for compulsory licence proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prima facie case is made to the satisfaction of the Board, the petitioner shall on or before a day named deliver to the patentee copies of the petition and affidavits/evidence; within 14 days the patentee shall leave affidavits/statutory declarations in opposition and deliver copies; within 14 days the petitioner shall leave affidavits in reply confined to matters strictly in reply; parties then heard under Board's directions with full opportunity to patentee to show cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register entries on sealing and changes of proprietorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon sealing of a patent the Comptroller shall enter in the Register of Patents the name, address and description of the patentee as the grantee and the title of the invention. Where a person becomes entitled to a patent or any share or interest by assignment, transmission, or operation of law, a request for entry of his name in the register shall be left at the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be signed/made by the claimant or authorised agent; particulars of the assignment/transmission showing manner and parties must be stated; supporting documents must be produced and an examined copy left (or an official/certified copy if matter of record). See Forms L and S.87/S.36 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of title documents for register entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Every assignment and every other document containing or being evidence of the title and transmission of a patent (except matters of record) shall be produced to the Comptroller together with the request, and such other proof of title as he may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters of record require an official or certified copy. An examined copy of the document shall be left with the request (Rule 69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate proprietorship registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A body corporate may be registered as proprietor by its corporate name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of 'Person' in S. 117 includes body corporate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and rectification on orders of Council or Court
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an order has been made by Her Majesty in Council for extension or grant of new patent, or by the Court for revocation or rectification of the register or otherwise affecting validity or proprietorship, the person in whose favour such order has been made shall forthwith leave an office copy at the Patent Office and the register shall be rectified or entry made accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S. 25 and S. 90 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of payments and failures in register
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issue of a certificate of payment the Comptroller shall enter in the Register of Patents the amount and date of payment. If a patentee fails to make a prescribed payment within the prescribed time or any enlargement thereof, such failure shall be entered in the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 45 and 73; see First Schedule for times of payment and Rule 46 for enlargement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of licences in register and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: An examined copy of every licence granted under a patent shall be left at the Patent Office by the licensee with a request that notification thereof be entered in the register; the licensee shall cause the accuracy of such copy to be certified as the Comptroller may direct, and the original licence shall be produced and left if required for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee for entry of licence referenced in First Schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection hours for the register
rubrics_metrics.description: The register of patents shall be open to the inspection of the public on every week day between the hours of ten and four, except on specified holidays, days notified by placard at the Patent Office, or times when the register is required for official use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copies of any entry in the register, or copies of certified copies or extracts from patents, specifications, disclaimers, affidavits, statutory declarations and other public documents in the Patent Office may be furnished by the Comptroller on payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee for office copies is 1d for every 100 words (but never less than 1s); the fee for certifying office copies is 1s each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to dispense with evidence or acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person is required to do any act, sign any document, make any declaration, or produce any document/evidence and is shown to the satisfaction of the Comptroller to be unable to do so for reasonable cause, it shall be lawful for the Comptroller, with the sanction of the Board of Trade and upon production of such other evidence and subject to such terms as they may think fit, to dispense with any such act, document, declaration, or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also S. 99 for further powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of previous general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All general rules made under the Patent Law Amendment Acts and in force on 31st December 1883 are repealed as from that date, without prejudice to any application then pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See S. 113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications and communications must be in English; no models required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and communications must be made in English. No models are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person, whether a British subject or not, may make an application for a patent; two or more persons may make a joint application; applications may be left at the Patent Office or sent prepaid by post addressed to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Places where stamped forms obtainable
rubrics_metrics.description: Stamped forms under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act, 1883 may be obtained at the Inland Revenue Office, Royal Courts of Justice, London General Post Office and many listed post offices throughout the United Kingdom, Scotland and Ireland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a 2s.6d impressed stamp is required (declaration before a Commissioner) the application form must be left with the Postmaster at one of the listed Post Offices who will get the form stamped; in London such forms can also be left at the Inland Revenue Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamp requirement for declaration before a Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The declaration required on application when made before a Commissioner requires a 2s. 6d. impressed stamp; the declaration before a justice of the peace requires no additional stamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the 2s.6d stamp is required the application form must be left with a listed Post Office for stamping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection application content and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for Provisional protection consists of: (a) the form of application, either Patent Form A or A1 (fee 1s each), and (b) the form of Provisional specification (Patent Form B) (gratis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should carefully read the directions upon the forms before filling them up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete protection application content and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for Complete protection consists of: (a) the form of application, either Patent Form A or A1 (fee 1s each), and (b) the form of complete specification (Patent Form C) (fee £3); total cost indicated as £4 in the Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a complete specification is filed after provisional has been allowed (within nine months of provisional application), the cost of the form for the complete specification is fee 3s (Patent Form C); a second application form is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing and agent communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'declaration' in the form of application must be signed by the applicant or applicants; all other communications may be made by or through agents duly authorized to the satisfaction of the Comptroller.
